measurement: FLAT DIFFERENTIAL — does the flat's dose difference reach the delivered object?
question: Two flats of the same optical state but different sky dose, applied to the SAME lights through the SAME chain: how much of the flats' difference survives to the delivered stack?
committed_before: the 125-frame arms. Written and committed BEFORE any arm of the real run is built.

full_disclosure_a_pilot_ran_first.why: The brief asserted 'both arms run identical frames through identical registration, so the two stacks are pixel-aligned'. That assertion is FALSE as the shipped builder stands, so a 12-frame pilot was run to test it BEFORE any prediction could be written. The pilot is disclosed in full here rather than hidden, because a pre-registration that conceals what was already seen is worth nothing.
full_disclosure_a_pilot_ran_first.what_it_falsified: register -2pass re-chooses the reference frame from image quality, and the CALIBRATION changes that choice. Measured, 12 frames of aug09/set-05, one knob (the flat): skyflat_set-05 -> reference image 1, canvas 4896x3616; skyflat_set-01 -> reference image 2, canvas 4887x3641. Two arms with different canvases are not pixel-comparable, and the reference choice is a SECOND knob.
full_disclosure_a_pilot_ran_first.the_fix_this_forced: run_undistort_pipeline.sh --regdata=<lt_.seq>: the first arm writes Siril's own registration data (per-image homographies + reference index), every later arm is handed that file and does not re-register. Transforms bit-identical across arms; the only difference in the products is the calibration.

pilot_numbers_already_seen.note: arm A's own stack reads FLAT (+0.0008) while the ratio against arm B reads -0.2352 — the registry's 'self-fulfilling flatness' in one line: the stack looks clean BECAUSE the flat absorbed the gradient.

full_disclosure_a_pilot_ran_first.determinism_measured_here_not_assumed: two unpinned rebuilds of the same 12-frame arm are BIT-IDENTICAL in pixels (0 differing pixels of 3x3616x4896; the md5 differs only in the header). So the identity control's floor is expected to be a TRUE ZERO, not a small number.

design.lights: aug09/set-05, 125 frames by EVEN STRIDE over the full 1497 s span (498 after the recipe cull). Even stride, never a contiguous block: the drift span is what smears the imprint and it is the quantity under test.
design.one_knob: the flat. Same raws, same master dark, same lens model, same warp, same registration data, same rejection, same stack normalization within a comparison.

arms.role: production calibration — the reference arm; writes the registration data
counterfactual dose — the banned cross-set manoeuvre, DIAGNOSTIC only
CONTROL 1a IDENTITY — same flat as A; the floor
CONTROL 1b UNIFORM — every pixel differs by 5%, the GRADIENT does not; the instrument must not respond
CONTROL 2 PLANTED — known edge ratio, opposite sign to the real signal
production normalization — An/Bn measures what the shipped chain absorbs

design.why_this_flat_pair: aug09 set-01 vs set-05 is the corpus maximum WITHIN a night (delta edge dipole 0.2827 against july31's 0.2152 and aug06's 0.1342). Within-night is REQUIRED, not convenient: focus recalibrates per session, so a cross-night pair differs in optical state as well as sky dose.
design.exemption_claimed: README step 1b bans cross-set flat reuse for DELIVERABLES. Arm B is that manoeuvre as a DIAGNOSTIC: tagged DIAGARM/CALXSET on the product itself, never delivered, never composed, never a verdict on a render.

inputs_measured_before_the_arms.instrument: scripts/qa/flat_odd_component.py — Siril fdiv + Siril stat regional medians, edge geometry box 80 / margin 2. No model, no fit.

flat_ratio_05_over_01.cross_check: LR 1.2955 reproduces the registry's directly-measured 1.2955 for this pair (four consecutive within-night increments multiply to 1.2944).

inputs_measured_before_the_arms.field_shape: corner_over_center 1.0108 says the ratio field is a near-LINEAR x-ramp with ~1% curvature; |dipole_x| is 12x |dipole_y|.

prediction.1_direction: arm B / arm A carries the SAME SIGN as the flats' ratio: edge_dipole_x NEGATIVE (left brighter), |dipole_x| >> |dipole_y|, dipole_y small and negative.
prediction.2_shape: a near-linear x-ramp; corner_over_center within 1.5% of 1.0; TB within 2% of 1.0.
prediction.3_upper_bound: |delivered| <= |flat ratio| = 0.2851. The delivered field is the flats' ratio SMEARED by the drift, and a smear cannot amplify.

4_smear_factor_stated_before_measuring.mechanism: each canvas point is the flux-weighted average of the ratio field over the sensor positions that sky point visited. For a LINEAR field the average equals the value at the MEAN sensor position, so the amplitude per pixel is unsmeared — what shrinks is the BASELINE, because -framing=min crops the canvas to the intersection of all frames' footprints.
4_smear_factor_stated_before_measuring.formula: factor = (W_canvas - 84) / (W_frame - 84), the separation of the edge boxes' centres (box 80, margin 2) on the canvas over the same separation on the 6064 px frame
4_smear_factor_stated_before_measuring.recompute_rule: the factor is recomputed from the 125-frame arm's OWN measured canvas before comparison. The canvas is measured independently of the ratio, so this is not a free parameter.
4_smear_factor_stated_before_measuring.caveat: for a field with curvature the canvas maps to an off-centre sensor window when the mean drift is non-zero, so a departure of a few percent is expected and is not a failure of the model.

prediction.5_two_instruments_must_agree: the matched-star flux differential (Siril psf aperture photometry at the same pixel in both arms) must return the same delivered edge-to-edge ratio as the pixel-ratio field, within the measured floor. Disagreement is the finding and gets attributed, never averaged.

6_controls.identity_A2_vs_A: ratio field EXACTLY 1.000 everywhere; every dipole exactly 0.0000; pixels bit-identical. Determinism is measured, not assumed — if it is not zero, something non-deterministic is in the arm and no number may be read until it is found.
6_controls.uniform_U_vs_A: level moves +5%, every dipole stays 0.0000. The instrument must respond to GRADIENT and not to LEVEL.
6_controls.planted_P_vs_A: the card is R(x) = 1 + 0.20*(x/W - 0.5), edge ratio 1.2222, whose own edge-geometry dipole is +0.1972 — POSITIVE, i.e. opposite in sign to the real signal, so a sign-blind artefact cannot fake it. Predicted delivered dipole_x = +0.1972 * factor = +0.1587 at the pilot canvas.
6_controls.discrimination_ratio: planted movement against the measured floor, the form the standard asks for (the iterative-flat NULL met 48-62x; the object-tilt instrument managed 0.20x and was unusable). With a floor of exactly zero the ratio is unbounded; the honest statement is then the floor's exact value and the count of quantities at which it is exactly zero.
6_controls.degeneracy_immunity: on object_tilt.py --selftest step 4a's PURE-TRANSLATION panel — where the absolute instrument returns -0.046 +- 0.0001 for a planted +0.100 and the lever collapses to 0.00 px — the DIFFERENTIAL fit must recover a planted flat difference correctly, because the per-star and per-block nuisances cancel identically in the difference and nothing is left free to absorb a linear mode.
6_controls.aperture_invariance: the photometric arm reports r = 10 and 16 px; a real throughput difference does not move with aperture, a PSF-fit artefact does.

7_normalization_absorption.confounder: -norm=addscale -output_norm computes per-frame coefficients from the frames' OWN statistics, which differ between arms because the flats differ.
7_normalization_absorption.reasoning_stated_before_measuring: in the registered domain each frame's window slides across the sensor by its drift, so the frame-mean of the ratio field varies with j and addscale removes that per-frame SCALAR. To first order in the ratio's amplitude, removing a per-frame constant leaves the canvas GRADIENT intact — the absorption should therefore be second-order, not the leading term.
7_normalization_absorption.why_it_is_worth_a_number_either_way: it says how much of a calibration difference the shipped chain silently swallows.

what_would_falsify_the_conclusion_that_t: the delivered ratio field's dipole_x is within the identity floor of zero (i.e. the flats' 0.2851 of contrast arrives as nothing)
the delivered dipole EXCEEDS the flats' own 0.2851 — that is physically impossible for a smear and would mean the arms differ by something other than the flat
the planted card is not recovered at the same smear factor as the real signal
the uniform card moves any dipole
the two instruments disagree by more than the floor and the disagreement cannot be attributed
scope_stated_before_the_result: This measures the DIFFERENCE of two imprints. A null BOUNDS the absolute object tilt (the object's sensitivity to a delta-dipole of 0.2851 would sit below the floor); it does not EQUAL the absolute tilt and cannot resurrect the 3.11% / 241-sigma figure, which stays UNVERIFIED. A positive result gives the delivered sensitivity to a KNOWN dose difference, which is the number a corrective needs. Neither outcome licenses a statement about the flat's share of the TOTAL defect; that stays UNTESTED per the registry.
